summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and anxiety was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 432 and an elevated anion gap. She was treated with IV fluids and insulin, which resolved her DKA. Persistent nausea was managed with antiemetics, and her tachycardia improved. Throughout the stay, she acknowledged that stress related to transitioning to an insulin pump contributed to her symptoms, and she recognized a pattern of self-induced vomiting during episodes. With support from her husband and medical team, she agreed to seek outpatient psychological care. By discharge, she was tolerating a soft diet, had no vomiting, and was stable. She was discharged home with medication adjustments and a plan for follow-up.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Personal history of peptic ulcer disease
